libraryPreparationPreflight.agent_guidance: Exercise StatsdMeterRegistry with a plain java.net.DatagramSocket bound to localhost on an ephemeral port as the 'StatsD server' (set via StatsdConfig.host()/port()) instead of a real StatsD/Datadog agent or Docker container — the wire protocol is just UDP text lines. Since publishing is async, poll/await the socket receive with a timeout rather than sleeping a fixed duration, and always call registry.close() in a finally block to stop the shaded reactor-netty client and avoid hanging the test JVM. When investigating the reported native-image bug, note the jar already bundles META-INF/native-image config for io.netty/io.projectreactor under their real (unshaded) coordinates — the gap is that the shaded class names (io.micrometer.shaded.io.netty.*, io.micrometer.shaded.io.netty.util.internal.shaded.org.jctools.*) aren't covered, matching the initialize-at-run-time and reflection metadata listed in the issue (DNS resolver holders, epoll/unix transport classes, JCTools MPSC queue field-offset classes). Confirm exact `initialize-at-run-time` needs by running native-image-agent trace plus fixTestNativeImageRun rather than copying the issue's list verbatim, since it was captured against a different Micrometer/Netty pairing (Micronaut, not this repo's harness).
risks: The reported failure ('stops publishing after running for a while') is a delayed/lazy class-initialization issue — a short-lived JVM/native-image test run may not trigger it, so coverage should specifically exercise the DNS-resolution and scheduled-task code paths the issue calls out, not just a single metric publish.

Shaded package layout can change between micrometer versions; verify class names against the actual 1.16.5 jar (already done here) rather than assuming the issue's Micronaut-reported list is exhaustive or current.
libraryPreparationPreflight.summary: All Netty/reactor-netty/JCTools classes referenced by the issue are shaded inside micrometer-registry-statsd itself (no separate dependency exists to add). Testing needs no Docker StatsD server or env vars — StatsdConfig.host()/port() can point at a local DatagramSocket. The real work is native-image metadata (initialize-at-run-time + reflection) for the shaded classes, which is the normal generation/fix workflow, not extra setup.
